title: iWorx
description: iWorx System Required System Specifications, Minimum 18-channel data recorder with the ability to expand to additional channels. Competing systems typically provide only 2-4 channels. Ability to gang multiple recorders together for expanded data acquisition. Includes 2 channels of wireless ECG/EMG and 3-axis accelerometer capability, with expansion to 16 wired channels. Competing products generally provide only 1-2 channels. Includes an ECG simulator. Integrated Pulse Oximetry, spirometry, grip force, and intensity sensors designed for enhanced measurement accuracy. Pre-calibrated temperature, force, spirometry, and blood pressure sensors, allowing immediate use with minimal setup requirements. Two built-in low-voltage input channels (+/-15V). Built-in isolated constant current high-voltage stimulator. Must be iWire compatible, allowing future expansion and integration of additional sensors and instrumentation. Expandable to a minimum of 34 total channels. Integrated barometric pressure sensor to improve spirometry accuracy without requiring separate external hardware. Minimum 16 digital I/O channels. Minimum 1 audio output channel. Portable design capable of operation through a USB-C power connection. Includes lifetime free LabScribe software updates and an open site license. Includes unlimited online training at no additional cost.

title: 6810--501 - Dry Ice Base +4
description: Introduction: This requirement is for delivery of 600 pounds of dry ice pellets every week for a total of 52 deliveries per year (31,200 pounds per year) for a five-year period. The Government intends to solicit quotations directly from SDVOSB suppliers without discussions with offerors. Therefore, the offeror s initial offer should contain the offeror s best terms from a price and technical standpoint. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if later determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary. The Government may reject any or all offers if such action is in the public interest; accept other than the lowest offer; and waive informalities and minor irregularities in offers received. The anticipated award date for this requirement is 12/01/2026. Background: The Cooperative Studies Program Clinical Research Pharmacy Coordinating Center s Biorepository in Albuquerque, New Mexico requires dry ice pellets for use when shipping biological samples. Required Services: A. Vendor will every week, on a Monday (unless Federal Holiday then vendor will deliver next day), deliver 600 lbs. of 5/8-inch dry ice pellets in a storage container. The storage container must keep sublimation to minimum possible level to maintain maximum useable quantity of dry ice. Acceptable performance standard is the weekly delivery of 600 pounds of dry ice pellets every week for a total of 52 deliveries per year and conformance standards are met. B. Vendor will pick up previously delivered container when delivering new container. Conformance Standards: Contract service shall ensure delivery containers meet applicable safety guidelines related to storage of dry ice. Storage container should be insulated with a hinged lid on casers designed for storage of dry ice pellets. This container is to be left at facility until the following delivery period. Container must be in good condition, fully operational casters, and lid. Container must also be free of damage or punctured insulation walls. Insulation walls of container will need to be a minimum of 2 1/2 inch thickness. Containers must have capability to hold a minimum of 700lbs of dry ice pellets. Lid must have a mechanism for holding the lid closed and in place. Containers must have a minimum of four casters, two that swivel, to support total weight of at least 700lbs of dry ice and allow for mobility across flat level surfaces. Loss due to sublimination should be less than eight percent (8%) of total mass every 24 hours. Common rule is 3-8% of total mass every 24 hours. Greater loss would be a result of inadequate or damaged containers. Hours of Coverage: Normal delivery hours are Monday through Friday from 7:30 am to 3:00 pm Mountain time. Deliveries must occur during normal delivery hours. Federal Holidays observed by NMVAHCS are: New Years' Day Labor Day Martin Luther King Day Columbus Day Presidents' Day Veterans' Day Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day Juneteenth Christmas Day Independence Day Other Pertinent Information or Special Considerations: Delivery Address/Point of Contact: Department of Veterans Affairs Cooperative Studies Program Clinical Research Pharmacy Coordinating Center 2401 Centre Ave SE Albuquerque, NM 87106 Points of Contact and Delivery Verification Steven Micklos, steven.micklos@va.gov, 505-265-1711 x6344 Paul Hicks, paul.hicks@va.gov, (505) 248-3206 We have our own free-standing facility detached from VA Hospital with loading/receiving dock. There is not a max radius location from vendor to delivery location as long as the integrity of the dry ice supply is not compromised in transit. Delivery Hours: 8:00am-3:30pm (MT) Delayed Orders: Delayed orders are not acceptable. Analyzing and testing biospecimens cannot be conducted as there would be no means to transport biospecimens while remaining viable for testing. Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be for one base year PLUS up to four (4) option years. The Government may extend the term of the awarded base/option year by written notice to the Contractor within 30 days of annual expiration date, provided that the Government gives the Contractor a preliminary written notice of its intent to extend at least 60 days before the contract expires. The preliminary (>60 day) notice does not commit the Government to an extension BASE YEAR CLIN Description QTY Unit 0001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB NOTE: CLIN is delivered in 52 separate deliveries (600 LB per delivery every week) OPTION YEAR 1 CLIN Description QTY Unit 1001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB OPTION YEAR 2 CLIN Description QTY Unit 2001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB OPTION YEAR 3 CLIN Description QTY Unit 3001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB OPTION YEAR 4 CLIN Description QTY Unit 4001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB

title: AK-AK MARITIME NWR-LEAK REPAIR
description: Please read the entire Request for Quotation (RFQ) and all attachments prior to submitting a quote. This is a Firm-Fixed-Price commercial purchase order. All responsible small business sources may submit a quote, which shall be considered by the agency. The basis of award is best overall value, determined by consideration of price and the other information described in the attached Offer Evaluation Information. Award will be made to a responsible source whose quotation represents the best overall value to the Government. This solicitation, 140FF027Q0080, is issued under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, including the simplified procedures at RFO 12.201-1, for heating system leak repair at the Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center, 95 Sterling Highway, Homer, AK 99603. Services shall be performed in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS 238220 - Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors, with a $19 million size standard, and PSC J045 - Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment - Plumbing, Heating, and Waste Disposal Equipment. Period of Performance: Date of award through 45 calendar days after award. All work shall be completed within 45 calendar days after award. Submit a completed and signed SF 1449, acknowledge any amendments, and provide the completed Bid Schedule with pricing for CLIN 00010 and a proposed completion schedule. Submit brief technical information demonstrating capability and approach to perform the Statement of Work, relevant commercial heating-system piping repair experience, and proof of the Alaska plumbing license required to perform the work. Include applicable quality-control information required by Section 7.1 of the Statement of Work. Include your SAM.gov Unique Entity ID and valid email address. Offerors must have active SAM registration with no exclusions. Identify any exceptions to the solicitation requirements; if none, state "None." Submit all offers via email to Tanner Frank: Tanner_Frank@ios.doi.gov. Email the SF 1449, completed B06 Bid Schedule, and Technical Submission as three individual PDF files. The email subject line must contain "RFQ 140FF027Q0080 AMNWR Heating System Leak Repair." Telephone calls are not accepted for offers or RFIs. title: Construction Services for Confined Aquatic Disposal Cell Construction and Maintenance Dredging of the Providence River Federal Navigation Project, Providence, Rhode Island.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a Sources Sought Announcement for the upcoming dredging project located in Providence, Rhode Island. This announcement is to determine the interest, availability and capability of Small and Large Business concerns as described below. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990. The solicitation for this project is anticipated to be issued on or about 15 March 2027. The construction will begin in September 2027 and is expected to take approximately 2 years to complete. The estimated construction cost is between $80,000,000 and $100,000,000. The Providence River Maintenance Dredging project involves two major sequences of dredging and disposal activities. The first work sequence will be the construction of a new Confined Aquatic Disposal (CAD) cell adjacent to the Providence River. The second work sequence under this contract will include maintenance dredging of the Providence River and Harbor Federal Navigation Project (FNP) to its authorized depths and dimensions. The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 5,500,000 cubic yards (cy) of material using closed clamshell buckets for both major sequences of work over the course of two years. The new CAD cell will be in the Edgewood Basin area located adjacent to the Providence FNP (hereafter the �Edgewood Shoals North (ESN) CAD cell�). To access the CAD cell area, an access channel will be dug between the Providence FNP and the CAD cell area. The access channel will be approximately 100 ft wide and -25 MLLW deep. The CAD cell will have surface dimensions of approximately 1000 ft. by 1000 ft. and be dug to a depth of -60 MLLW. The material excavated to build the access channel is generally a mix of sandy silt and shell fragments. Within the CAD cell area the material is generally described as soft grey to black organic silt with some layers of firm sandy silt and some shell fragments and coarse-grained material. Material excavated from the access channel and CAD cell area will be placed at four locations: Port Edgewood Basin, the Fox Point Reach CAD cells, Prudence Island Disposal Site, and the Rhode Island Sound Disposal Site. This work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,200,000 cy to construct thew ESN CAD cell and its access channel, which must be completed before maintenance dredging of the FNP can begin. The maintenance dredging proposed work consists of mechanically dredging the Providence River FNP to the full -40 MLLW depth plus 2-feet of allowable overdepth. 2,300,000 cy (1,200,000 cy required depth, with up to 1,100,000 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting generally of poorly graded medium to fine sand with silt. The dredge material from this maintenance portion of work will be placed in the ESN CAD cell. Environmental coordination and permitting is being completed by the U.S. Army of Engineers, New England District. All dredging and disposal activities for this project have prescribed work windows that incorporate environmental and recreational time of year restrictions. Refer to the Draft Specification Section provided with this announcement for specifics on the time of year work restrictions. In order to accomplish all dredging requirements within the specified dredging window it is expected that the Contractor will need to meet a production rate of 300,000 CY per 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is requesting responses to the questions below from both small and large businesses[MC1] . Draft drawings showing a concept design plan and draft Specification Section of 01 11 00 SUMMARY OF WORK have been provided with this announcement to help provide more context for the contract work and responses to these questions. Considering the different disposal locations, are there suggestions on a bid structure that will provide for the most accurate costs of different disposal locations? Any draft restrictions that may impact dredging and/or disposal operations? Any concerns on the period of performance of September 2027 to September 2029 considering the environmental windows and amount of work? If so, why? Any comments about the bed leveling planned in the Fox Point Reach? Are there concerns about this part of the plan, if so, why? Interested firms should also demonstrate their project experience, by providing two (2) projects within the last ten years, which meet the following requirements: Dredging by mechanical means demonstrating a minimum production rate of 300,000 cubic yards in one consecutive 30-day period. Experience with placement of dredged material at an open water placement site in New England during the fall/winter months of October through March. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, etc.), type of equipment the firm is proposing to use on the project, and two (2) example projects performed by the firm in the last ten (10) years (including Points of Contact for those projects) showing experience with the proposed equipment at the production rate listed above. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications meeting the same qualifications listed above, which will be used to support the bidder's effort. Firms may use subcontractor experience to demonstrate experience with the requirements, but the role and work performed by each team member (prime and subcontractors) on projects demonstrating that team member's experience shall be the same as the role for that team member for this project. Bid bond will need to be provided with the bid. Responses are limited to twenty pages and due by November 26 , 2026. Responses should be addressed to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District, 696 Virginia Road, Concord, MA 01742-2751, ATTN: Kyle Hall, or electronically to Kyle.K.Hall@usace.army.mil. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. Government Agency URL: www.nae.usace.army.mil Government Agency URL Description: New England District, Corps of Engineers

title: Rakennusurakointitöiden puitehankinta vuosille 2027-2029
description: Rakennusurakointitöiden puitehankinta vuosille 2027-2029 Naantalin kaupungin yksiköt (Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia rakennusurakointitöiden toteuttamisesta sopimuskaudelle. Hankinnan kohteena olevat työt toteutetaan joko erikseen minikilpailutettavina toimeksiantoina tai suoraan hankittavina töinä sopimusehtojen mukaisesti. Rakennusurakoita kilpailutetaan lisäksi kohdekohtaisilla urakkakilpailulla. Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.1.2027. Lisäksi Tilaaja varaa mahdollisuuden kahteen optiovuoteen (1+1). Optiolla tarkoitetaan mahdollisuutta sopimuksen jatkamiseen alkuperäisin ehdoin. Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä erikseen. Hankinta tullaan toteuttamaan puitejärjestelynä. Tilattavien töiden sisältö ja määrä eivät ole ennalta tiedossa eikä Tilaaja sitoudu mihinkään hankintamääriin sopimuskauden aikana. Pienurakat voivat sisältää rakennus-, maalaus-, matto-, tasoite-, vedeneristys- sekä laatoitus- ja teräsrakennetöitä. Urakat toteutetaan noudattaen rakennusalan yleisiä sopimusehtoja YSE 1998.,

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Planungsleistungen für ein Nahwärmenetz der Leistungsphasen 2 – 4 in den Quartieren Gildekamp und Gotthunkamp in der Stadt Röbel/Müritz.
description: Die Stadt Röbel/Müritz erwägt den Neubau eines innovativen Nahwärmenetzes in den Quartieren Gildekamp und Gotthunskamp mit Potential zur Erweiterung und damit zum Anschluss anderer Quartiere der Stadt. Das Ziel ist der Aufbau einer zukunftssicheren, CO2-mindernden und wirtschaftlichen Wärmeversorgung der Stadt Röbel/Müritz in Teilabschnitten bis 2045. Dabei sind die Anforderungen, die sich aus dem Wärmeplanungsgesetz vom 20.12.2023 § 30 Abs. 1 und § 31 Abs. 1 ergeben einzuhalten. Gegenstand der zu vergebenden Leistung ist die Erbringung der stufenweisen Planungsleistungen gemäß § 53 der Leistungsphasen 2 bis 4 HOAI (Vorplanung, Entwurfsplanung, Genehmigungsplanung) für das Nahwärmenetz Röbel, unter Beachtung der Anforderungen der BEW-Förderrichtlinie (Fassung vom 16. Dezember 2025). Die Leistungen müssen die im BAFA-Merkblatt („Bundesförderung für effiziente Wärmenetze – Merkblatt Antragstellung, technische Anforderungen und Verwendungsnachweis) definierten Mindestinhalte nach Ziffer 4.2.3 vollständig abdecken.

title: RFI Process control system plumbing and programming
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army DEVCOM Soldier Center to identify potential sources to provide expert engineering support to trouble shoot process control system providing steam water and air. Must have expertise in process control plumbing and control valves for steam systems. Must have expertise in Allen Bradley PLC programming. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to mary.k.prebensen.civ@army.mil and Wesley.s.shaw.civ@army.mil by November 26th, 2026 by 5pm EST. Background: The Government (DEVCOM Soldier Center) is in need of expert engineering support to diagnose current PLC and piping system which support multiple hydraulic press systems. The existing system controls water, steam and air to molding tooling, and the PLC operates on custom Allen-Bradley control software. As it stands, the system is physically installed, however does not provide necessary temperature control in either manual or automatic modes. Issues may be traced to the original system design, pipe rack installation, PLC programming or some combination of the three. Description: Expert engineering services are sought to diagnose newly installed PLC control system to ensure that it can meet system design requirements, can be operated safely and reliably, and is adaptable for future operation and changing requirements. A new PLC system has been designed and installed per a list of system requirements, however is not able to control temperature per design requirements either due to control logic, poor valve selection or related piping design/installation. SC requires a 3rd party engineering service to validate as-built drawings against the installed system, verify/update PLC programming, provide necessary hardware changes to bring the system up to full operability. Specific System Specifications: Electric steam boiler provides 125psi dry steam as primary heat source for molding tooling. Standalone chiller provides chilled water at ~60 psi, and house air provides air for purge and mist functions. The Allen-Bradley PLC system controls the various media through a series of modulating valves to heat or cool the tooling. The PLC is intended to have recipe writing and management for automated control. Basic recipe for our process includes steam heat via pressure control to desired temperature setpoint, hold for ~1 hr while controlling temperature. The tooling is then cooled with chilled water at a controlled cooling rate. Our standard tooling includes an upper and lower platen, and the PLC has capability to control these independently. Additional system requirements will be included if there is a future RFP. Current known system issues: System will not maintain equivalent temperature for upper and lower platens during heat up or hold. System will not control cooling rate based on system feedback loop. System trend screen not displaying data correctly. System alarms remain untested. Mist function does not function without vibration of piping rack. Unique Vendor qualifications: Potential vendor must be US based and employ US citizens identified to work on the PLC system due to sensitivity of materials and products produced by the installation laboratory. Potential vendor must be licensed in process system design with specific expertise in steam controls. Potential vendor must be able to read modify and update Allen Bradly system code. Deliverables: Full system walkdown and comparison to As-built drawings. Analysis of system design, layout, valve selection, PLC operability as compared to provided list of system requirements. List of proposed design changes to meet system requirements and cost of implementation. Install required hardware and make required changes to system software. May subcontract for implementation of hardware changes. Provide updated As-built drawings for plumbing systems, electrical systems, PLC controls systems. System demonstration and verification to the As-built drawings provided Modified code in digital and hardcopy. Verified system manual. Full system demonstration and minimum 1 day training on system operation. Delivery Date: Government estimates work will be completed within 6 months of date of contract award. Government Furnished Property (Equipment/Materials/Information/Computer Utilization): All work to be performed on site at SC with access to existing PLC and piping rack. description: Outdoor Fitness Facility, Building 389� Supply, Delivery, and Limited Installation Support Notice Type: Sources Sought / Market Research Notice Number: HARBSS-2027-01 Contracting Office: 482d CONF/PK Location of Performance: Homestead Air Reserve Base, Florida Response Due Date/Time: November 26, 2026, 5:00 PM EST Response Submission: Nika Salemi, nika.salemi.2@us.af.mil Proposed NAICS Code: 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Proposed Product Service Code (PSC): 5670 Building Components, Prefabricated 1. Notice Purpose THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED FOR MARKET-RESEARCH AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR QUOTATION, INVITATION FOR BID, OR COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO AWARD A CONTRACT. The 482d Contracting Flight, Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), FL, seeks information from capable commercial sources, including all small-business socioeconomic categories, to determine the availability and capability of firms that can perform the requirement described in Attachment 1 KYJM19-9003 Outdoor Fitness SOW, Red Horse Project, 12 Nov 2026. Responses will be used to support acquisition planning, including consideration of the appropriate contract type, acquisition approach, and potential small-business set-aside strategy. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparation or submission of information in response to this notice. A response to this notice is not required to respond to a future solicitation, if issued. Any future solicitation will be announced separately. 2. Requirement Overview The 482d Contracting Flight, Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), FL is conducting market research for the Outdoor Fitness Facility, Building 389 project at Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), Florida. The anticipated requirement is primarily for the procurement, delivery, and associated submittals for construction materials and equipment required to support construction of an outdoor fitness facility. Air Force RED HORSE personnel will perform the majority of construction and installation activities. Contractor installation responsibilities are limited principally to the steel picket fence and, if applicable, a separate lightning-protection system. The contractor would be expected to: Procure and deliver all materials identified in the Government-furnished bill of materials (BOM), Attachment 2 Outdoor Fitness Facility, BOM Template. Furnish the Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) package, including engineered shop drawings and all associated structure materials. Coordinate concrete-truck deliveries to support Government construction execution. Furnish the specified construction equipment for the required durations, fueled and ready for operation at the work site. Install a new steel picket fence, including site restoration for areas disturbed by fence installation. Install a lightning-protection system if the proposed PEB cannot include a compliant built-in lightning-protection system. The provided BOM identifies, among other materials and equipment, rubber fitness flooring, concrete masonry materials, electrical distribution materials, outdoor fans, motion-activated lighting, concrete, base course, PEB-related items, and construction-equipment rentals. 3. Anticipated Scope 3.1 Material Procurement and Delivery The contractor shall be capable of procuring, delivering, and warranting the materials and equipment identified in the Government-furnished BOM. The contractor shall provide required material and equipment submittals before ordering materials, and the Government will approve final submittals in writing before purchase. Anticipated submittals include: Steel picket fence; PEB signed and sealed shop drawings; Outdoor ceiling fans; Lighting; Smart meter; Electrical panel; Fitness flooring; Bird netting; Material warranty plan, including roof, flooring, and other applicable equipment warranties; and Fence material and labor warranty. 3.2 Pre-Engineered Building Package The contractor shall be capable of providing a complete PEB material package based on Government design drawings, including digitally signed and sealed shop drawings prepared by a Professional Engineer. The PEB package is expected to include, at a minimum: Lifting-rack/support beams; A fixed steel beam with predrilled holes for 25-foot ropes; Toe-hold bars located three inches above the finished floor; Factory coating and painting, with Government-selected colors; Medium-bronze exterior roof panels and manufacturer-standard light interior roof panels; Standing seam metal roofing; Gutters and downspouts; Built-in copper lightning protection, where available; and Black, heavy-duty polyethylene bird netting with �-inch mesh meeting or exceeding the specified mesh-quality and break-strength requirements. The PEB shall be designed in accordance with the SOW�s specified structural and high-velocity-wind requirements. The SOW requires a minimum 20-year material warranty, a current Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance for the PEB and insulation, and a roof assembly capable of the stated uplift and wind criteria. Zinc-plated metal is prohibited. 3.3 Lightning Protection System � Conditional Installation If a compliant PEB with built-in lightning protection is unavailable, the contractor shall be capable of furnishing and installing a conventional lightning-protection and grounding system following completion of RED HORSE construction activities. The contractor�s capability should include: Copper lightning-protection materials; Installation shop drawings; UL-listed and labeled components; Fence-bonding connections; Grounding-system testing and test-point documentation; Third-party inspection and written certification by an entity independent of the system designer and installer; and Compliance with the project�s cited lightning-protection requirements. 3.4 Steel Picket Fence Installation and Site Restoration The contractor shall be capable of furnishing and installing a steel picket fence around the outdoor-fitness-facility overhang structure. The fence must be located at least five feet from the roof overhang and include an accessible, lockable gate/door. The fence-related scope includes required access and equipment doors, hardware, and restoration of disturbed areas using St. Augustine sod. 3.5 Construction Equipment The contractor shall be capable of furnishing the construction equipment identified in the BOM for the stated rental periods or project duration. Anticipated equipment includes a 12,000-pound telehandler forklift, skid loaders with buckets and forks, a water truck, scissor lifts, straight-track manlifts, a double-drum roller, a mini excavator with hammer, a dump truck, and concrete forms with pins. Equipment shall be delivered to the project site, fueled, and ready for operation. The contractor will not be responsible for subsequent refueling unless otherwise established in a future solicitation. 3.6 Installation Access and On-Site Requirements Potential sources should be capable of working on an active military installation and complying with applicable installation access, identification, safety, security, and operations-security requirements. For contractor-performed installation work, the contractor must be capable of providing an English-fluent site superintendent who remains on site during contract performance. Excavation, if required, will require coordination and permits before work begins; the SOW specifies that permit requests must be submitted at least three weeks before excavation. Normal anticipated work hours for fence installation are 0730�1630, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays, unless alternate hours are approved in writing. 4. title: RFI Process control system plumbing and programming
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army DEVCOM Soldier Center to identify potential sources to provide expert engineering support to trouble shoot process control system providing steam water and air. Must have expertise in process control plumbing and control valves for steam systems. Must have expertise in Allen Bradley PLC programming. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to mary.k.prebensen.civ@army.mil and Wesley.s.shaw.civ@army.mil by November 26th, 2026 by 5pm EST. Background: The Government (DEVCOM Soldier Center) is in need of expert engineering support to diagnose current PLC and piping system which support multiple hydraulic press systems. The existing system controls water, steam and air to molding tooling, and the PLC operates on custom Allen-Bradley control software. As it stands, the system is physically installed, however does not provide necessary temperature control in either manual or automatic modes. Issues may be traced to the original system design, pipe rack installation, PLC programming or some combination of the three. Description: Expert engineering services are sought to diagnose newly installed PLC control system to ensure that it can meet system design requirements, can be operated safely and reliably, and is adaptable for future operation and changing requirements. A new PLC system has been designed and installed per a list of system requirements, however is not able to control temperature per design requirements either due to control logic, poor valve selection or related piping design/installation. SC requires a 3rd party engineering service to validate as-built drawings against the installed system, verify/update PLC programming, provide necessary hardware changes to bring the system up to full operability. Specific System Specifications: Electric steam boiler provides 125psi dry steam as primary heat source for molding tooling. Standalone chiller provides chilled water at ~60 psi, and house air provides air for purge and mist functions. The Allen-Bradley PLC system controls the various media through a series of modulating valves to heat or cool the tooling. The PLC is intended to have recipe writing and management for automated control. Basic recipe for our process includes steam heat via pressure control to desired temperature setpoint, hold for ~1 hr while controlling temperature. The tooling is then cooled with chilled water at a controlled cooling rate. Our standard tooling includes an upper and lower platen, and the PLC has capability to control these independently. Additional system requirements will be included if there is a future RFP. Current known system issues: System will not maintain equivalent temperature for upper and lower platens during heat up or hold. System will not control cooling rate based on system feedback loop. System trend screen not displaying data correctly. System alarms remain untested. Mist function does not function without vibration of piping rack. Unique Vendor qualifications: Potential vendor must be US based and employ US citizens identified to work on the PLC system due to sensitivity of materials and products produced by the installation laboratory. Potential vendor must be licensed in process system design with specific expertise in steam controls. Potential vendor must be able to read modify and update Allen Bradly system code. Deliverables: Full system walkdown and comparison to As-built drawings. Analysis of system design, layout, valve selection, PLC operability as compared to provided list of system requirements. List of proposed design changes to meet system requirements and cost of implementation. Install required hardware and make required changes to system software. May subcontract for implementation of hardware changes. Provide updated As-built drawings for plumbing systems, electrical systems, PLC controls systems. System demonstration and verification to the As-built drawings provided Modified code in digital and hardcopy. Verified system manual. Full system demonstration and minimum 1 day training on system operation. Delivery Date: Government estimates work will be completed within 6 months of date of contract award. Government Furnished Property (Equipment/Materials/Information/Computer Utilization): All work to be performed on site at SC with access to existing PLC and piping rack. Notice Purpose THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED FOR MARKET-RESEARCH AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR QUOTATION, INVITATION FOR BID, OR COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO AWARD A CONTRACT. The 482d Contracting Flight, Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), FL, seeks information from capable commercial sources, including all small-business socioeconomic categories, to determine the availability and capability of firms that can perform the requirement described in Attachment 1 KYJM19-9003 Outdoor Fitness SOW, Red Horse Project, 12 Nov 2026. Responses will be used to support acquisition planning, including consideration of the appropriate contract type, acquisition approach, and potential small-business set-aside strategy. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparation or submission of information in response to this notice. A response to this notice is not required to respond to a future solicitation, if issued. Any future solicitation will be announced separately. 2. Requirement Overview The 482d Contracting Flight, Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), FL is conducting market research for the Outdoor Fitness Facility, Building 389 project at Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), Florida. The anticipated requirement is primarily for the procurement, delivery, and associated submittals for construction materials and equipment required to support construction of an outdoor fitness facility. Air Force RED HORSE personnel will perform the majority of construction and installation activities. Contractor installation responsibilities are limited principally to the steel picket fence and, if applicable, a separate lightning-protection system. The contractor would be expected to: Procure and deliver all materials identified in the Government-furnished bill of materials (BOM), Attachment 2 Outdoor Fitness Facility, BOM Template. Furnish the Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) package, including engineered shop drawings and all associated structure materials. Coordinate concrete-truck deliveries to support Government construction execution. Furnish the specified construction equipment for the required durations, fueled and ready for operation at the work site. Install a new steel picket fence, including site restoration for areas disturbed by fence installation. Install a lightning-protection system if the proposed PEB cannot include a compliant built-in lightning-protection system. The provided BOM identifies, among other materials and equipment, rubber fitness flooring, concrete masonry materials, electrical distribution materials, outdoor fans, motion-activated lighting, concrete, base course, PEB-related items, and construction-equipment rentals. 3. Anticipated Scope 3.1 Material Procurement and Delivery The contractor shall be capable of procuring, delivering, and warranting the materials and equipment identified in the Government-furnished BOM. The contractor shall provide required material and equipment submittals before ordering materials, and the Government will approve final submittals in writing before purchase. Anticipated submittals include: Steel picket fence; PEB signed and sealed shop drawings; Outdoor ceiling fans; Lighting; Smart meter; Electrical panel; Fitness flooring; Bird netting; Material warranty plan, including roof, flooring, and other applicable equipment warranties; and Fence material and labor warranty. 3.2 Pre-Engineered Building Package The contractor shall be capable of providing a complete PEB material package based on Government design drawings, including digitally signed and sealed shop drawings prepared by a Professional Engineer. The PEB package is expected to include, at a minimum: Lifting-rack/support beams; A fixed steel beam with predrilled holes for 25-foot ropes; Toe-hold bars located three inches above the finished floor; Factory coating and painting, with Government-selected colors; Medium-bronze exterior roof panels and manufacturer-standard light interior roof panels; Standing seam metal roofing; Gutters and downspouts; Built-in copper lightning protection, where available; and Black, heavy-duty polyethylene bird netting with �-inch mesh meeting or exceeding the specified mesh-quality and break-strength requirements. The PEB shall be designed in accordance with the SOW�s specified structural and high-velocity-wind requirements. The SOW requires a minimum 20-year material warranty, a current Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance for the PEB and insulation, and a roof assembly capable of the stated uplift and wind criteria. Zinc-plated metal is prohibited. 3.3 Lightning Protection System � Conditional Installation If a compliant PEB with built-in lightning protection is unavailable, the contractor shall be capable of furnishing and installing a conventional lightning-protection and grounding system following completion of RED HORSE construction activities. The contractor�s capability should include: Copper lightning-protection materials; Installation shop drawings; UL-listed and labeled components; Fence-bonding connections; Grounding-system testing and test-point documentation; Third-party inspection and written certification by an entity independent of the system designer and installer; and Compliance with the project�s cited lightning-protection requirements. 3.4 Steel Picket Fence Installation and Site Restoration The contractor shall be capable of furnishing and installing a steel picket fence around the outdoor-fitness-facility overhang structure. The fence must be located at least five feet from the roof overhang and include an accessible, lockable gate/door. The fence-related scope includes required access and equipment doors, hardware, and restoration of disturbed areas using St. Augustine sod. 3.5 Construction Equipment The contractor shall be capable of furnishing the construction equipment identified in the BOM for the stated rental periods or project duration. Anticipated equipment includes a 12,000-pound telehandler forklift, skid loaders with buckets and forks, a water truck, scissor lifts, straight-track manlifts, a double-drum roller, a mini excavator with hammer, a dump truck, and concrete forms with pins. Equipment shall be delivered to the project site, fueled, and ready for operation. The contractor will not be responsible for subsequent refueling unless otherwise established in a future solicitation. 3.6 Installation Access and On-Site Requirements Potential sources should be capable of working on an active military installation and complying with applicable installation access, identification, safety, security, and operations-security requirements. For contractor-performed installation work, the contractor must be capable of providing an English-fluent site superintendent who remains on site during contract performance. Excavation, if required, will require coordination and permits before work begins; the SOW specifies that permit requests must be submitted at least three weeks before excavation. Normal anticipated work hours for fence installation are 0730�1630, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays, unless alternate hours are approved in writing. 4. Reque

buyer: European Commission, DG REGIO - Regional and Urban Policy
title: Belgium – Business and management consultancy and related services – Learning through Experimentation for Adaptive Programming (LEAP) - Producing experimental designs for ERDF/CF/JTF investment in the field of access to quality public services
description: The overarching goal of this assignment is to prepare the ground for embedding experimentation in National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs) from the outset of the 2028–2034 programming period. To this end, the assignment will structurally bring evaluators and programmers to work together, build capacity on both sides, and provide the EU evaluation system with practical experimentation tools that extend beyond the three participating MS. This assignment focuses on investments on access to public services and shall produce the following outputs: 1. NRPP-ready experimental designs to be implemented in the 2028–2034 programming period in three Member States; 2. a detailed toolkit to support MS in the introduction of experimental designs in 2028-2034 Plans: LEAP Kit (Learning through Experimentation for Adaptive Programming). Access to quality public services is central to the Right to Stay initiative and to the social and territorial cohesion objectives of the EU. Ensuring that services remain within reach of citizens, particularly in lagging and rural regions, is increasingly challenging as budgets tighten and demographic pressures intensify. The constraint is often not only that infrastructure is missing or outdated, but its accessibility and quality is not up to standards. The question of intervention approaches in this regard is underexplored and poorly evidenced. Experimentation through randomised controlled trials (RCTs) - and the analysis of experiment results to identify the causal effects of interventions - offers the most rigorous way to generate this evidence. Improving the capacity to design and conduct experimental designs is even more important in light of the evolving regulatory context. The Commission proposal for the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework explicitly promotes policy learning and experimentation as a function of both coordinating and managing authorities (Articles 50 and 51 of the proposed Performance Regulation). DG REGIO’s ambition is that experimental designs and adaptive learning mechanisms will be embedded in the NRPPs from the outset of the next programming period.

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Neubau Verwaltungsgebäude der Verbandsgemeindewerke in Bernkastel-Kues / Andel: Los 1 - Leistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Freianlagen
description: Gegenstand der Planungsaufgabe ist der Neubau eines Verwaltungsgebäudes der Verbandsgemeindewerke in Bernkastel-Kues im Stadtteil Andel einschließlich der zugehörigen Freianlagen und der Einbindung in den bestehenden Betriebsstandort auf dem Grundstück "Moselbahnstraße 14 in 54470 Bernkastel-Kues / Andel". Für das Vorhaben liegt bereits ein erster Konzeptentwurf vor, der als Grundlage für die weitere Planung dient. Der derzeitige Planungsstand sieht ein zweigeschossiges Verwaltungsgebäude mit einem Brutto-Rauminhalt (BRI) von ca. 3.061 m³, einer Brutto-Grundfläche (BGF) von ca. 840 m², einer Netto-Raumfläche (NRF) von ca. 604 m² sowie einer Nutzfläche (NUF) von ca. 410 m² vor. Das Raumprogramm umfasst im wesentlichen Büroarbeitsplätze für technische und kaufmännische Bereiche sowie Besprechungs-, Kommunikations-, Sozial-, Technik- und entsprechende Sanitär- und Nebenräume. Der vorliegende Konzeptentwurf sieht eine flexible und langfristig anpassbare Gebäudestruktur in einem klaren Baukörper vor, in einer zeitgemäßen und energieeffizienten Bauweise. Ein zentraler, über die beiden Geschosse offener Lichthof innerhalb der Erschließungszone bildet den räumlichen Mittelpunkt des Gebäudes und dient der Belichtung, Kommunikation und natürlichen Belüftung der angrenzenden Bereiche. Die einzelnen Funktionsbereiche im Gebäude "Büros/Besprechung", "Erschließung" und "Nebenräume" sind klar gegliedert, gleichzeitig entsteht über die Mitte des Gebäudes und den Lichthof eine offene Kommunikationszone mit Aufenthaltsqualität. Wesentliche Entwurfsziele sind eine hohe Nutzungsflexibilität und langfristige Anpassungsfähigkeit der Grundrissstruktur sowie kurze, funktionale Wege innerhalb des Gebäudes und eine gute Anbindung und Sichtbeziehung an das bestehende Betriebsgebäude auf dem Grundstück. Der beauftragte Objektplaner hat die bisherige Konzeption und das zugrunde liegende Raum- und Funktionsprogramm gemeinsam mit dem Auftraggeber zu überprüfen, gegeben falls weiterzuentwickeln und mit den beteiligten Fachplanern abzustimmen. Dabei sind insbesondere Funktionalität, Wirtschaftlichkeit, Nachhaltigkeit, Energieeffizienz und die langfristige Nutzungsflexibilität, aber auch eine differenzierte Fassadengestaltung zu berücksichtigen. Mit Wirkung zum 01.01.2027 werden die Verbandsgemeindewerke Bernkastel-Kues in die Verbandsgemeindewerke AöR umgewandelt. Die AöR übernimmt alle Rechte und Pflichten der Verbandsgemeindewerke Bernkastel-Kues. Hinsichtlich der Einzelheiten wird Bezug genommen auf die beigefügte Leistungsbeschreibung Bezug genommen, welche Bestandteil der Vergabeunterlagen/Vertragsunterlagen ist.

title: Germany – Education and training services – Rahmenvereinbarung über fachbezogene Nachhilfe (Deutsch und Mathematik) zur Lernförderung an Startchancen-Schulen im Land Brandenburg (Los 6)
description: Das auf insgesamt zehn Jahre angelegte und am 01.08.2024 gestartete Startchancen-Programm (SCP) des Bundes und der Länder soll dazu beitragen, den Bildungserfolg von der sozialen Herkunft zu entkoppeln. Grundsätzliches Ziel ist die Verbesserung der Basiskompetenzen in Deutsch und Mathematik der Schülerinnen und Schüler. Zur Unterstützung der Zielerreichung beabsichtigt das Ministerium für Bildung, Jugend und Sport (MBJS) des Landes Brandenburg, eine fachbezogene Nachhilfe für die Unterrichtsfächer Deutsch und Mathematik als Zentralmaßnahme für alle interessierten Grundschulen, Förderschulen, weiterführenden allgemeinbildenden Schulen bis Jahrgangsstufe 10 (darunter insbesondere Oberschulen) und Beruflichen Schulen (darunter insbesondere Oberstufenzentren = OSZ) zu beauftragen. Um den Schulen bedarfsabhängige Nachhilfeangebote je Schulhalbjahr zur Verfügung stellen zu können, soll eine Rahmenvereinbarung geschlossen werden. Abrufberechtigte werden die losweise benannten Schulen sein. Gegenstand dieses Loses (Los 6) ist die Region Region Dahme-Spreewald, Märkisch-Oderland (außer Bad Freienwalde) und Fürstenwalde/Spree mit acht Schulen. Ziel der Maßnahme ist es, die schulischen Leistungen der Schülerinnen und Schüler nachhaltig so zu verbessern, dass sie die durch den Rahmenlehrplan Jahrgangsstufe 1-10 definierte Niveaustufe ihrer Jahrgangsstufe am Ende des Schuljahres erreichen. Nähere losspezifische Angaben sowie Angaben zur konkreten Ausgestaltung der Nachhilfeleistungen sind dem Dokument Leistungsbeschreibung (Anlage 13) zu entnehmen.

title: Belgium – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Assessing the Elasticity of Retail Investment to Tax Incentives
description: The study should pursue two complementary objectives. First, it should estimate the elasticity of retail investment to tax incentives by analysing in order to determine how strongly tax advantages affect the likelihood to invest and the amounts invested. Second, it should assess the potential budgetary implications of introducing an SIA under different design scenarios, taking into account varying forms of tax incentives participation rates and substitution effects with existing savings products. This second objectives should be possibly combined with an assessment of second round effect of greater retail participation to capital markets on consumption and investment.. Taken together, the study should allow policymakers to assess the cost effectiveness of SIAs as a tool to increase retail participation in capital markets under the Savings and Investments Union.

description: Umeå kommun avser att upphandla ett nytt PA-system till Kulturhuset Väven. title: Sweden – Vending machines – Upphandling av hyra av varuautomater för nikotin- och tobak till Statens institutionsstyrelse
description: SiS inbjuder till anbudsgivning gällande Upphandling av hyra av varuautomater för nikotin- och tobaksprodukter för SiS LVM-hem enligt nedanstående instruktioner och bifogade handlingar med diarienummer 2.2-9233-2026. Avrop kommer att genomföras i enlighet med upphandlingsdokumenten. Bakgrund Många klienter som får vård- och behandling på SiS LVM-hem har behov av att genomföra inköp av nikotin- och tobaksprodukter under sin tid på hemmen. Eftersom klienterna ofta har begränsade möjligheter att lämna institutionsområdet så avser SiS nu att upphandla ramavtal för hyra av varuautomater. Syftet med upphandlingen är att underlätta införskaffandet av och bidra till att effektivisera och förenkla inköp av nikotin- och tobaksprodukter för klienter som själva genomför köpen inom institutionsområdet. Uppdragsbeskrivning Upphandlingen avser hyra av varuautomater för nikotin- och tobaksprodukter inklusive teknisk service och påfyllnad av produkter. Med teknisk service avses att anbudsgivaren ansvarar för alla tillstånd för att sälja nikotin- och tobaksprodukter, att alla lagkrav på både försäljning och automater efterlevs samt för service, reparationer, rengöring, hantering av reklamationer, svinn och annat som krävs för att säkerställa en god driftsäkerhet och funktion. Avropsberättigande enheter är SiS samtliga LVM-hem. Avrop genomförs vid behov av respektive LVM-hem. Behov av sortiment i varuautomaterna kan komma att skilja mellan olika LVM-hem, till exempel olika utbud av nikotin- och tobaksprodukter såsom cigaretter och snus. Avtalsvärdet för denna upphandling är satt till 9 000 000 SEK och takvolymen är begränsad till 11 000 000 SEK. SiS garanterar inga volymer, anbudsgivare åtar sig att leverera mot det faktiska behov som uppstår. Ovanstående angivna värden utgör endast en vägledning. Det framtida behovet kan komma att understiga ovan angivna takvolymer. Preliminär avtalsperiod är från och med 2026-12-16 till och med 2028-12-15. Beställaren har därefter rätt, men ej skyldighet, att förlänga Avtalet med ett (1) år i taget i totalt två (2) år. Avtalsperioden kan därmed löpa som längst till och med 2030-12-15. Avtalet förlängs per automatik med ett (1) år i taget om inte Beställaren meddelar annat senast tre (3) månader innan Avtalet löper ut.

title: Sweden – Tutorial services – Handledartjänster
description: Upphandlingen omfattar konsultstöd av handledartjänster. Syftet med handledning är att med hjälp av extern kompetens stödja medarbetare i yrkesrollen med kunskap och stimulans till lösningar. Stödet ska stärka medarbetaren och bidra till att utveckla arbetsgrupper i metoder och förhållningssätt i det kontinuerliga arbetet med olika brukargrupper. Stödet ska också ge möjlighet till reflektion och förståelse av sig själv och andra människor.Medarbetarna ska bland annat få stöd i att hantera svåra situationer i arbetet och få reflektera över arbetet, sig själv och den professionella rollen i ett tryggt forum där alla ges utrymme. Handledningen ska bidra till att medarbetarna får mental avlastning och ny energi och på så sätt motverka känslomässig utmattning. Upphandlingen omfattar handledning inom följande anbudsområde: Anbudsområde 1: Socialtjänst Utredningsinstitution, Ärendehandledning, uppdragsbaserade föräldrautredningar. Handledningen ska i första hand ske på plats. Anbudsområde 2: Socialtjänst Handledning inom individ- och familjeomsorg. Anbudsområde 3: SocialtjänstHandledning för budget-och skuldrådgivare. Anbudsområde 4: SocialtjänstHandledning för socialsekreterare ekonomiskt bistånd. Anbudsområde 5: SocialtjänstHandledning inom LSS och socialpsykiatriÄrendehandledning utifrån behov hos medarbetare som arbetar nära brukare. Anbudsområde 6: SkolverksamhetYrkesprofessionell handledning för skolkuratorer inom elevhälsan riktat mot grundskola och gymnasium. Anbudsområde 7: Skolverksamhet Yrkesprofessionell handledning för skolsköterskor, skolläkare och logopeder inom elevhälsan riktat mot grundskola och gymnasium. Anbudsområde 8: Skolverksamhet Yrkesprofessionell handledning för psykologer inom elevhälsan riktat mot grundskola och gymnasium. Anbudsområde 9: Arbetslivsinriktad rehabiliteringProcesshandledning i kombination med konsultation samt undervisning kring olika psykiska, sociala, kognitiva och språkliga funktionshinder. Personalen ska utbildas och handledas i professionell psykologisk coaching.

title: USCG Station at Cape Disappointment
description: General. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT and is for informational/market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTATION OR BID, NOR A SYNOPSIS OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION UNDER RFO FAR SUBPART 5.1, PRESOLICITATION. This Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of industry so the government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small business members of industry to include: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). All interested parties are highly encouraged to respond. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is: TBD - The approximate value of Project will be $50M to $100M. Formal Sources Sought Response Due � before 3:00 pm PDT on 26 November 2026 2. Project Details and Background. The USCG Station at Cape Disappointment requires repairs, upgrades, and improvements to existing infrastructure and nearby areas to restore and retain full mission readiness. The Station is on an unstable sandbar which has experienced sediment migration into dock and adjacent waterway areas. Dock structures are failing and require repair/replacement. The vessel haul-out facility is currently inoperable due to sedimentation and requires the USCG to conduct frequent maintenance dredging. Haul-out structure is failing and requires replacement. Adjacent landscape features pose rockfall dangers above the engineering and maintenance buildings to people and property 3. Project Scope. Rockfall slope instability corrective measures: Anticipated rockfall mitigation will require corrective measures including but not limited to tree removal, rock scaling, rock dowel installation, draped mesh removal and replacement, removal and/or repair of an existing damaged ringnet fence, and installation of a midslope attenuator system. Rockfall mitigation will require difficult access techniques to reach the full height of the hazardous slope. Temporary protection of the facility and workers will be required. Repairs to damaged roadways, utilities or access pathways may be required. Repair of an existing small landslide slump along the access road is required. Final mitigation work will reduce rockfall risk to USCG personnel and facility. Waterfront structures and vessel haul-out: The waterfront structures require repairs and upgrades. Replacement of the existing floating docks is required; they will retain their current configuration (footprint) but utilize updated material specifications. Existing timber and steel piles will be either replaced, or reused with new floats, as part of this contract, depending on current condition. Geotechnical, civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical scope is included. Constraints include: Float A to be retained; guide piles at floating docks #2 and #4 to be replaced; wave screens to be replaced; electrical equipment to be upgraded; existing vessel haul-out facility to be replaced. Eel grass and SAV surveys are required to inform design. Dock operations are to be maintained during construction, per phasing to be outlined by the government. Coastal Resilience and Sedimentation Remediation: Due to the catastrophic loss of the protective coastal dune, the facility requires a comprehensive permanent solution to control massive sediment migration. Bathymetric surveys, geotechnical testing, and coastal modeling are required to inform viable design and permit alternatives. The design will utilize modern, resilient coastal engineering practices including Nature-Based Solutions (NBS), dynamic revetments, segmented offshore breakwaters/sills, and the beneficial reuse of dredged sediment wherever practicable. Construction may be implemented in functional phases to optimize funding and operational readiness. Shoreline protection repairs and upgrades are considered part of this category along with the Haul Out structure. Interim repair work: Interim repair work may be required on existing structures before new design and construction activity can be completed. If the need arises, USACE will provide USCG a description of the recommended repairs and a cost estimate. If USCG would like USACE to institute repairs, an updated agreement to define the scope will be established. 4. Submission Instructions. Formal responses to this Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically via MSForms (link is here https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/Aivta2iThu) for answers to Section 3 Questions above and via email with supporting documentation requested here in Section 4 Submission Instructions. Submit your email with SUBJECT: "Response to questions on Cape Disappointment". Please email to Brandon Lasich Brandon.M.Lasich@usace.army.mil and Jaren Bowman, at jaren.l.bowman@usace.army.mil Interested parties� responses to this Sources Sought shall be limited to six (6) pages and shall include the following information: What is the interest in submitting a proposal for a Design Build solicitation for the dock work What would be the interest in submitting a bid for a Design Build solicitation for the Sedimentation mitigation work. What is the interest in submitting a proposal for a Progressive Design Build contract. Provide benefits and risks for Progressive Design Build for any of the scope items presented. What issues do you see with soliciting for construction contracts work as described in section 3. List the capabilities of your firm to do the design and construction of new segmented breakwater and haul structure working close to a Federal Channel, complex tidal currents and wave loading, complex movement of sand, and subject to large storm event What are the capabilities to design and construction for the renovation of new dock work. Do you have experience designing to USACE and/or USCG waterfront design criteria: USCG Configuration Standard Technical Orders relevant to this project scope UFC/USACE requirements relevant to this project scope Design for complex hydro loading conditions in shallow bays to USACE/UFC criteria. List previous design build work for doing work in complex environment where one had to consider the working close to a Federal Channel, complex tidal currents, complex movement of sand, subject to large storm events and is highly dynamic. List previous design build work for dock work. What issues do you see with the work. What issue do you see with design bid build. Provide input for benefits and negatives to separate construction contracts (for each scope item in Section 3), or a combination of scope items into 1 or 2 contracts. Rockfall Mitigation Specific Questions What construction methods are anticipated for the rock scaling, for rock dowels, mesh and attenuator installation? What is the general anticipated construction sequence to remove trees, scale rock and debris, install mitigation and make repairs to existing rockfall systems (to remain)? How will rock scaling be performed? What method(s) will prevent scaled rock and cut trees from damaging building, buried utilities? What are the anticipated types and size of equipment required to construct the rockfall systems - e.g. crane or helicopter size; wagon drill, crane mounted drill, or hand plugger; scale bar, air bag, or mechanical scaling, etc? List any constructability issues or concerns; e.g. accessibility, equipment footprints, scaling etc. What is the contractor�s experience with similar types of flexible midslope attenuator/geohazard mitigation on transportation, dam infrastructure or similar projects? During rockfall mitigation work, how fast can work stop, safely hold and clear road debris to allow USCG emergency responders full, safe access to execute rescue operations? Dock R
